turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_htsteel_retention_train.csv: 55 real samples, columns
    process/composition columns (Fe, Cr, Ni, Mo, Mn, C, Ti, Si, Nb, V, P, B,
    Al, Cu, W, S) and `target` (the measured hot-strength retention ratio
    YS(600C)/YS(20C)).
  - b3_htsteel_retention_pool.csv: 26 CANDIDATE samples whose hot-strength
    retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C) was NOT measured, columns
    `candidate_id` and the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST hot-
strength retention ratio YS(600C)/YS(20C), then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I would prioritize **c019, c015, c020, c011, and c013**, using composition similarity to the strongest training samples. With only 55 observations, these are approximate predictions; the ordering of closely ranked candidates is uncertain.

| Rank | Candidate | Approximate retention ratio | Training-data basis |
|---:|---|---:|---|
| 1 | **c019** | **0.95** | Closely resembles the high-Ni, Ti/W-containing samples with measured ratios **1.000** and **0.875**. Its Ni ≈35%, W ≈3.2%, and substantial Ti/Al make it a strong candidate within this high-retention composition family. |
| 2 | **c015** | **0.92** | An especially close match to the low-alloy sample with **0.9375** retention: Cr 0.50%, Mo 0.50%, Mn 0.55%, and C 0.12%, versus this candidate’s 0.55%, 0.50%, 0.55%, and 0.125%. |
| 3 | **c020** | **0.90** | Also resembles that **0.9375** sample, particularly in Mo content and low Cr/Ni. Its higher Mn and somewhat higher carbon introduce more uncertainty than for c015. |
| 4 | **c011** | **0.88** | The strongest direct analogue contains Cr 11.25%, Ni 23%, and Ti 2.9%, with measured retention **0.9032**. This candidate retains the same Cr and Ti, but has lower Ni and no Mo, warranting a modestly lower estimate. |
| 5 | **c013** | **0.84** | Closely related to the Ni 26.9%, Ti 1.16%, Al 1.23%, W 2.97% sample with retention **0.8214**. It preserves this composition family while adding Mo, although the data do not establish a reliable independent Mo benefit. |

These estimates are **analogue-based judgments, not outputs from a fitted, validated model**. In particular, c020 and c011 could exchange places. **c004** is the closest alternative to the selected five, but c013 has stronger similarity to the measured high-retention Ni–Ti–Al–W samples.

Final: c019, c015, c020, c011, c013
